output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. Over the previous 26 weeks the average was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher than this one. Each was investigated and no fault was found. The 34% jump looks large only because it is a percentage of a small number. The dashboard matches the raw logs, and it hasn't been edited. Bookings were flat, and support logged no complaints.

The new-pod versus old-pod gap (0.52% against 0.30%) isn't evidence against v4.18. The same gap shows up in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of the old image. New pods start with a cold cache, and that causes about 10–20 extra timeouts per rollout. That is far too few to explain the weekly rise.

I can't rule out the replica move or partner-sync traffic, but nothing requires them to explain the rise. I'm fairly confident in this.

What to do: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would disable the burn-rate page, which is the protection that catches real problems. Note the week as normal at ops review and apply the standard check next week. Separately, consider warming caches on new pods during rollouts.
